content:
As WhatsApp officially launches its username feature, the app now allows users to store usernames in addition to names and phone numbers when saving contacts. Here are the details.

The new username field feature is being gradually rolled out to some WhatsApp users

Although usernames are a basic feature on most instant messaging platforms, WhatsApp has only recently begun to move away from relying entirely on phone numbers to identify users.

WhatsApp earlier this year began rolling out a username reservation system, allowing users to register their desired usernames in advance to prevent impersonation and scams when the feature officially launches.

Several weeks ago, WhatsApp began enabling the username feature for some iPhone users.

According to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp has begun supporting users in filling in the username field when adding contacts. This field appears between the first and last name fields and the phone number field.

WABetaInfo reports:

WABetaInfo points out that the username field appears to be gradually rolling out to specific users on WhatsApp Beta and the stable version.

When I tested using the latest stable version, although the field was displayed, the system still showed a message saying "This username is not on WhatsApp" even though the username actually exists.

That said, this marks WhatsApp finally catching up with its competitors by adding a feature that many believe should have been introduced long ago.
